Win Conditions & Team Comps

Every team has a plan that wins. Learn to spot your team's win condition, the five comp types, drafting basics, and how to play from ahead and from behind.

What a win condition is

A win condition is the simplest answer to the question: "How does our team win this game?" It might be "our Jinx gets three items and we protect her", or "our Fiora split pushes top while we hold mid", or "we poke them down before fights with Ziggs and Xerath".

When you know your win condition, decisions get easier. Every time you're unsure what to do, ask whether it helps the plan. Should the support ward bot side or follow the jungler? Should you fight now or wait? The win condition decides.

Look for it during loading screen. Check both teams and ask: who on our team scales best, who is ahead, and what does our comp do well?

The five team comp types

Most team compositions fall into one of these, or mix two:

CompHow it winsExample champions
Engage (dive)Jumps on the enemy team with big crowd control and wins the 5v5.Malphite, Leona, Orianna
Poke (siege)Damages enemies from long range until they're too low to fight, then takes objectives.Ziggs, Xerath, Jayce, Ezreal
PickCatches one enemy out of position, kills them, then forces an objective 5v4.Ahri, Thresh, Ashe
Protect (front-to-back)Keeps one hyper-carry alive while they deal all the damage.Jinx, Lulu, Karma
Split pushOne strong duelist pushes a side lane while the team stalls, forcing the enemy to split up.Fiora, Jax, Twisted Fate

Each comp beats some and loses to others. Engage beats poke (you jump on them before they can poke you down). Poke beats protect (the hyper-carry gets chipped before the fight). A good pick comp punishes split pushers. Know which one you are and which one they are.

Common mistakePlaying against your comp. A poke team that walks into a 5v5 face-to-face fight with an engage team will lose even if it's ahead in gold.

Drafting basics

In ranked you pick your champion in champ select. A few simple rules:

  • Pick what you're good at. A champion you've played 100 times beats the "perfect" pick you've never played.
  • Look at your team's damage. If your team has four physical damage champions, a mage helps a lot. Otherwise the enemy just builds armor.
  • Make sure someone can start a fight (hard crowd control) and someone can stand in front (a tank or bruiser).
  • Counter-pick if you're picking late, but only with a champion you know.
  • Ban what you hate playing against, or what's strongest right now (check our tier list).
Pro tipHave a "safe" champion for each role that's hard to counter. When you're forced to pick first in your role, play that one.

Playing from ahead

Being ahead feels good, but many games are thrown here. When you're ahead:

  • Turn kills into objectives. After winning a fight, take a turret, Dragon or Baron immediately. A kill with no objective is a wasted lead.
  • Take vision of their jungle. Push their side of the map and ward deep, so they can't farm safely.
  • Don't fight in their territory without vision. Being ahead doesn't protect you from walking into five people in a bush.
  • Group and force objectives. Make them fight you at Dragon or Baron, where your lead matters most.

Playing from behind

Games are rarely over at 20 minutes. When you're behind:

  • Farm safely. Catch waves under your own turrets and let your scaling champions catch up.
  • Don't contest everything. If you can't win a fight at Dragon, give it and take something on the other side instead.
  • Look for picks. Enemies who are ahead get overconfident and walk into your jungle alone. Wait in vision-free bushes.
  • Remember comeback rewards. Bounties on fed enemies and extra experience from objectives for the losing team can swing a game fast.

The team that's behind wins by waiting for one mistake. Be patient and ready.

Closing out the game

The best time to end is right after you win a big fight or take Baron. Steps:

  1. Win a fight or take Baron.
  2. Push the closest lane with your whole team and the big minion wave.
  3. Take inhibitors. With inhibitors down, super minions keep pushing for you.
  4. Back, buy, and come again before they respawn. Don't stay too long with low health.

Death timers get long late in the game (up to about 79 seconds). Count how many enemies are dead and how long until they respawn before you go for the Nexus.

Key takeaways

  • Your win condition is the simplest plan for how your team wins. Find it in loading screen.
  • Know your comp type (engage, poke, pick, protect, split) and play to it.
  • Pick champions you know well and make sure your team has mixed damage and crowd control.
  • When ahead, turn every kill into an objective. When behind, farm safely and wait for a mistake.
  • End right after a won fight or Baron. Don't stay too long.
